reason: Owner requested premium finish upgrade matching lobby design language
outcome: Successful installation. Wood frames met energy performance spec. No structural issues at 8 units.
lessons_learned: Wood frames from Premium Wood Co. (Jane Miller) delivered on time at 4-week lead. Structural weight review not triggered below 8 units. FSC certification provided same day. Total cost delta: $2,000 (8 units x $250 premium). Smooth execution — good precedent for similar substitutions.

reason: Subcontractor proposed vinyl as cost-saving substitution
outcome: Rejected. Vinyl frames fail wind load rating above 3rd floor per RULE-012.
lessons_learned: Vinyl is not spec-equivalent for exterior use above floor 3. Any vinyl substitution above 3rd floor must be rejected outright. RFI issued to architect confirmed non-approval. 5-day schedule delay while alternative was sourced.

reason: Wood frames in high-traffic lobby showing premature wear; aluminum provides better durability
outcome: Accepted. Aluminum replacement installed without structural concerns. Lobby aesthetics maintained.
lessons_learned: Reverse substitution (wood to aluminum) for high-traffic ground floor areas is straightforward. AlumaCraft delivered in 3 weeks. Net cost saving of $1,500 vs. wood equivalent. Drawing markup A-101 issued and approved same day.

reason: Steel stud shortage from supplier; wood stud available from local supplier
outcome: Accepted with conditions. Non-load-bearing partition only. Structural engineer confirmed equivalence.
lessons_learned: Non-load-bearing wall stud substitution is low-risk if PE confirms non-structural. Quick turnaround — decision made same day. Cost delta minimal.

reason: Hardwood flooring supply chain delay; LVP available immediately
outcome: Rejected. Owner rejected LVP as spec-downgrade despite cost savings. Hardwood sourced from alternate supplier.
lessons_learned: Owner has strong preference for spec-equivalent or better materials. LVP perceived as downgrade even though waterproof performance is superior. 10-day delay from rejected substitution. Always escalate finish material changes to owner rep.

reason: CMU lead time 12 weeks; LGSF available in 4 weeks
outcome: Rejected. Structural engineer determined LGSF insufficient for exterior wind loads at this building height.
lessons_learned: Structural material substitutions always require PE review before any other steps. Bypassing structural review wastes time on infeasible proposals. RULE-004 must be enforced strictly.

reason: AHJ inspection flagged ground-floor glass as non-compliant with IBC safety glazing requirements
outcome: Accepted immediately. Mandatory code compliance upgrade. No approval threshold applies.
lessons_learned: Code compliance changes bypass normal approval thresholds. PM can approve unilaterally. Tempered glass for ground floor is now standard spec going forward.

reason: Fire marshal required Type X throughout corridor assemblies to meet 1-hour fire rating
outcome: Accepted. Mandatory fire code compliance. Cost absorbed in contingency.
lessons_learned: Fire rating upgrades are non-negotiable. Cost impact absorbed in project contingency (no change order needed). Schedule delay manageable. Always flag fire-rating changes as critical path.

reason: Owner design change — minimalist aesthetic preferred
outcome: Accepted. Polished concrete is lower cost and easier to maintain. Net cost savings.
lessons_learned: Owner-driven design changes with cost savings are easy approvals. Polished concrete reduces future maintenance costs. Owner rep (Robert Hayes) approved in under 2 hours.

reason: Design consistency with 5th floor upgrade (EVT-001); owner requested matching premium finish throughout
outcome: Accepted. Same wood frame supplier (Premium Wood Co., Jane Miller). Structural weight review confirmed acceptable below threshold.
lessons_learned: Second aluminum-to-wood window substitution in project. Established process from EVT-001 made this very smooth. Premium Wood Co. familiar with project spec. 4-week lead time confirmed. FSC certs on file.

reason: PM identified moisture damage risk from painted drywall in bathrooms; tile is moisture-resistant
outcome: Accepted. Proactive improvement to prevent future water damage claims.
lessons_learned: Cost $45,000 — required PM + Owner approval per RULE-002. Robert Hayes approved after PM presented moisture damage risk analysis. Close to $50K escalation threshold — worth noting for future similar scope.

reason: Project-wide window upgrade to wood frames for sustainability certification (LEED points)
outcome: Accepted pending structural review. Lisa Wong confirmed 12-unit wood frame weight acceptable for post-tensioned 4th floor slab.
lessons_learned: Third aluminum-to-wood window upgrade. Quantity of 12 triggered structural weight review per RULE-008. Lisa Wong completed assessment in 1 day. 6-week lead time applied per RULE-005. Premium Wood Co. PO issued immediately after structural sign-off. Direct precedent for 3rd floor scenario.
